item.title: Goats at the Arboretum
item.description:
Tuesday, August 4, 2026 at 7 AM

August 4-11, 2026 – Dates are subject to change. Please check back for updates.7:00 am – 7:30 pm Goats from GoatScaping LLC will be at the Arboretum this August clearing out invasive and aggressive native understory brush and vegetation to allow for increased biodiversity! This year, the goats will be working on a 7 acre area in the northwest corner of the Arboretum between the 610 Parking Loop, the Ravine Trail, and the Event Lawn. Read below for some helpful tips for viewing the goats at work! Are you an Arboretum Member? If so, join us on Friday, August 7 from 10:00 am – 12:00 pm for a fun, free Members-only Meet the Mowers event! 2026 Goat visit map Goat Viewing Tips Park at either entrance and look at the Goat Visit Map to plan your walk. Stay on sidewalks and trails. Keep children and dogs away from the fence – it is electrified to keep predators like coyotes out of the area. Do not try to feed or pet the goats. They are helping us clear species like poison ivy, and the oils can get on your skin. Take lots of photos – if you post them on social media, tag @houstonarboretum so we can see them!

From Houston Arboretum & Nature Center

item.title: HXD Week: Power Hour
item.description:
Wednesday, August 5, 2026 at 8 AM

Location: 20 E. Greenway Plaza, 20 E. Greenway Plaza, Suite 525, Houston, TX, 77046, United States

The Place for Creatives: In an AI Evolving World As artificial intelligence continues to reshape the way we work, the value of distinctly human skills has never been greater. As routine analytical tasks become increasingly automated, creativity, strategic thinking, collaboration, and innovation are emerging as the true drivers of business success. For the Architecture & Design industry, this shift raises an important question: What does the future look like for the creative worker, and what kind of workplace helps them do their best work? Join a panel of leading design professionals as they explore how the workplace is evolving beyond a place to complete tasks into an ecosystem that fosters connection, inspires creativity, and accelerates innovation. Together, they’ll discuss how thoughtful workplace design can empower creative talent and support the next generation of work. Moderator Steve Kopp, AIA, ACHA CannonDesign Steve Kopp brings more than 20 years of expertise to his role as a Design Leader, focusing on the design of pediatric, academic health, and research facilities. He is recognized for leading teams through complex design challenges to deliver innovative, sustainable, and cost-effective solutions. A dedicated advocate for evidence-based practice, Steve leverages materiality and strategic planning to improve outcomes for every user group he serves.     Panelists Necia E. Bonner, RID, NCIDQ, IIDA, CHID, CDF, LEED AP Principal, Director of Health & Science Interiors Perkins&Will Necia Bonner is a Principal and the Director of Health & Science Interiors for Perkins&Will’s Houston studio, where she leads interior design strategy for some of the most complex healthcare, research, and science environments in the country. With more than 25 years of experience dedicated exclusively to high-performance interiors, she has worked across a broad spectrum of specialized facilities, including academic medical centers, community hospitals, behavioral health facilities, public health agencies, private clinics, research laboratories, vivaria, and corporate science campuses. A Certified Healthcare Interior Designer and Certified Design Futurist, Necia is recognized for her expertise in translating complex clinical, operational, and regulatory requirements into innovative environments that support the future of healthcare delivery and scientific discovery. She is a respected leader within the design profession and a frequent advocate for advancing healthcare and science environments through design leadership, education, and professional service. Necia has served in numerous leadership roles with IIDA, the AIA Committee on Architecture for Health, the Texas Association for Interior Designers, and currently serves on the board of Texas Women in Healthcare.   Megan Funni, RID Assistant Professor of Practice Sam Houston State Universty Megan Funni is an Assistant Professor of Practice at Sam Houston State University, where she teaches across the interior design curriculum. She also does contract furniture and commercial interior design work with Maybe Sometimes Studio. With more than 16 years of commercial design experience, including work with Fortune 500 companies and Class A landlords, Megan brings both professional practice and academic perspective to her work.       MacKenzie Greckel Balden Contract Group MacKenzie Greckel is a sales representative with Balden Contract Group (BCG) in Houston’s commercial design community and the artist behind GRECK. With a background in the fine arts, she brings a creative perspective to every aspect of her work, blending art, design, marketing, and sales. Passionate about building relationships and thinking beyond traditional industry norms, MacKenzie enjoys finding unconventional ways to connect creativity with the commercial design world.       Morgan Dougherty SHSU Student & McCoy Rockford Design Intern Morgan is an emerging interior designer from Houston, Texas with a passion for creating innovative spaces that enhance the way people work, live, and connect. While completing her degree in Interior Design at Sam Houston State University             Garth Williams Technical Director PDR As PDR’s Technical Director, Garth and oversees the documentation, permitting and construction observation of all PDR projects in addition to setting the firm’s design technology and project delivery standards. He brings fourteen years of experience in commercial interiors to PDR’s Design + Architecture studio and his industry knowledge and technical background allow him to recognize and resolve efficiency gaps in the design and documentation process and ensure that all aspects of an issue are thoughtfully considered when providing guidance to the studio. Garth has extensive architectural experience in the legal, financial and oil & gas markets as well as a background in information technology, BIM, sales, and marketing. This varied breadth and depth of experience allows him to recognize architectural, organizational, and technical solutions to a variety of issues. As Technical Director, Garth guides all project teams in the Design + Architecture studio, reviewing drawings, providing guidance on building codes and accessibility, developing documentation standards and creating new tools and processes. Garth expertly interprets concepts and ideas and implements them in a way that benefits the studio, and ultimately, PDR’s clients.   Parking: Surface lot parking available. – Located on the east side of the building with entrances on Norfolk St. and Portsmouth St. – After parking, proceed to check-in with security located in the building lobby. – Please be ready to provide your driver’s license and vehicle information. While our physical street address is “20 E Greenway Plaza, Houston, TX 77046”, searching the address will lead to the wrong location. To avoid routing issues, we recommend searching for “Twenty Greenway Plaza, Houston, TX 77046” rather than entering the street address. We’ve found that searching the building name generally provides more accurate results across Google Maps, Apple Maps, and Bing Maps.

From AIA Houston

item.title: HXD Week: The Power of Brain Health in Workplace Wellbeing
item.description:
Wednesday, August 5, 2026 at 12 PM

Location: Perkins&Will, 1001 McKinney St, 19th Floor, Houston, TX, 77002, United States

In an era where productivity, innovation, and resilience are the keys to success, the state of our brains, our cognitive function, mental clarity, and emotional well-being play a crucial role in how we perform at work. Yet, in the hustle of deadlines, meetings, and constant digital demands, we often neglect the very organ that drives our success: the brain. What if we told you that small, science-backed changes in your daily routine could boost your focus, reduce stress, and enhance overall job satisfaction? Imagine a workplace where mental fatigue is minimized, creativity flows naturally, and employees thrive, not just survive. This session will dive into a topic that affects every aspect of our professional and personal lives: brain health and workplace wellbeing. Building on the research shared by one of the facilitators at the United Nations European Brain Health Summit, we’ll explore the neuroscience behind optimal brain health, practical strategies to enhance cognitive function, and how organizations can design and foster an environment that supports mental well-being. By the end, the audience will have actionable insights & sited examples to not only improve their own performance but also contribute to a healthier, more productive workplace. AIA credit: 1.0 HSW/LU Presenter: Julie Gauthier, IIDA, RID, LEED AP Associate Principal, Workplace, Houston Perkins&Will Workplace Practice Lead at the Houston Studio of Perkins&Will, Julie embraces beauty and function in all aspects of her role as an interior designer. Every day, she is driven by conceptualizing client-focused, functional, and healthy environments that are built upon communication, strategic programming, and a passion for creating spaces that inspire. Julie also pairs her design practice with advisory services, having championed new initiatives for workplace strategy, design for wellbeing, sustainability tracking, and change management.    Lunch: Catered lunch will be provided. Please register well in advance before registration closes to secure your lunch. Email Alex Moreno (alexm@aiahouston.org) with any dietary restrictions. Parking: Please input the address for 900 Fannin into your GPS and it will take you straight to the parking garage. If you use 1001 McKinney, you will have trouble locating it. You will pull a parking ticket upon entry and use the same ticket to exit. You may park in any unreserved space on the 5th floor and above. Note that our garage is marked for 1001 McKinney at the entrance. We are not at the McKinney Place parking garage. Thank you, and we look forward to your visit at the Perkins&Will Houston Studio! Please bring your parking ticket inside with you for validation. Feel free to call the front desk at 713-366-4000 if you need assistance.

From AIA Houston

item.title: Summer Venture Studio Preview Day @ Ion District
item.description:
Wednesday, August 5, 2026 at 3:30 PM

Location: Ion – Forum Stairs, 4201 Main St., Houston, TX, 77002, United States

Register here: https://luma.com/6jbyeu9f Check-in begins at 3:30 PM. Event begins at 4:00 PM. Be among the first to see what’s next 👀 ​Join us for the inaugural Summer Venture Studio Preview Day, where this year’s cohort of ambitious student founders will pitch the ventures they’ve spent the summer building. ​Hosted by the Ion District and in partnership with Rice Alliance, SVS Preview Day is both a showcase and a celebration of Houston’s innovation community. ​Meet founders, connect with fellow entrepreneurs, investors, mentors, and supporters, and help us celebrate the next generation of student innovators at Rice. ​Meet the 2026 SVS Cohort! ​Actile Technologies ​Founder: Barclay Jumet ​Actile develops wearable smart fabrics that communicate critical information through the language of touch, helping operators’ eyes and ears stay focused on their environment in national defense and other demanding settings. ​DHI Tech ​Founders: Dev Sanghvi, Madhuvani Thatiparti, Aneesh Thatiparti ​DHI Tech is developing a plug-and-play edge AI layer for surveillance networks that makes every camera a smart device, covering 25-plus safety, compliance and security use cases out of the box. ​Kairos Health ​Founders: Adhira Tippur, Sanjana Kavula, Tanush Chintala, Aditya Jain ​Kairos have developed an AI-powered patient intake platform built specifically for independent dental practices. ​Lucero Health ​Founders: Halbert Kim, Rohan Dharia ​Lucero connect patients to supplemental resources, turning non-medical needs into actionable care beyond the clinic via a digital platform. ​MedIQ Health ​Founders: Suran Somawardana, Jacob Lei, Patrick Bednarz ​MedIQ is developing hardware and software solutions that help asthma patients and their doctors better manage their condition. ​Codene ​Founders: Adam Towner, Saul Brauns ​Codene are building the AI platform for go-to-market engineering. They Codene discovers ideal customers, executes personalized outreach and accelerates the journey from launch to revenue. ​Vantage ​Founders: Gavin Firestone, Nolan Connolly ​Vantage have developed an AI motion coach that uses computer vision to deliver instant, actionable feedback on exercise technique and programming. ​Magma Health ​Founder: Ramtin Shahzanian ​Magma clones real companies into high-fidelity RL environments. ​Coop ​Founders Adithiya Balaguru, Arnav Bhalla ​Coop are building an early respiratory disease detection system for poultry farms using AI to analyze audio feeds collected from poultry houses. ​Learn more ​About Summer Venture Studio ​Summer Venture Studio (SVS) provides an immersive three-month experience where Rice student entrepreneurs receive $15,000 in non-dilutive funding, individualized mentorship, workspace and access to an extensive network of experienced founders, investors, and industry experts. ​Since launching in 2023, SVS has become one of Rice’s premier pathways for translating student innovation into high-growth companies. More than half of participating ventures have gone on to raise pre-seed or seed financing, while alumni companies have earned acceptance into some of the world’s most competitive accelerators programs, including Y Combinator and Tech Stars. ​For more information, visit Lilie Summer Venture Studio! ​About Liu Idea Lab for Innovation & Entrepreneurship (Lilie) ​The Liu Idea Lab for Innovation and Entrepreneurship (Lilie) is the home for entrepreneurship and innovation at Rice University. As the center for entrepreneurship on campus, Lilie runs courses and co-curricular programs to help develop students, researchers, faculty, and alums into entrepreneurs for life.

From Ion District

item.title: Characterizing the role of Nephronectin during Anterior Eye Development in Mice
item.description:
Wednesday, August 5, 2026 at 7 PM

Location: Keck Hall

  Speaker: Matthew Robert Garis Doctoral Candidate Thesis Defense Department: BioSciences-Biochemistry and Cell Biology Location: Keck Hall 102 Anterior eye development is a complex process involving the migration, proliferation, patterning and interactions between many difference cell types in order to achieve the niche tissue properties required for proper sight. The periocular mesenchyme interacts with nascent ocular tissues and extracellular matrix proteins to provide a transparent cornea. While support structures like sensory nerves and anterior eye vasculature are formed and patterned with tight spatiotemporal regulation to sustain ocular structures. Cellular interactions with the extracellular matrix are essential in regulating these morphogenic processes, but which specific component proteins achieve these effects and the signaling pathways involved are not well understood. These studies were developed to further understand the role of the extracellular matrix protein nephronectin (Npnt) during anterior eye development. While the protein has been researched during avian cornea development, its role in mice was yet to be described. The method by which these two organisms develop the cornea varies greatly and this opened the potential to discover species-specific functions of Npnt. To this end, I utilized a Npnt mutant mouse model to probe how the murine cornea is formed without this matrix protein. I show that Npnt is utilized as a migration substrate by the periocular mesenchyme (POM), as its absence leads to a reduction in corneal thickness and decreased cell counts but does not affect proliferation capacity. This result was confirmed via in vitro POM explant experiments demonstrating the ability for these cells to use Npnt as a substrate to migrate upon and blocking the EGFR pathway abolished that capacity. Thus, I found Npnt to mediate the migration of POM cells into the murine cornea during development by activation of the EGFR pathway. Npnt has been shown to play a role in angiogenesis and sensory nerve patterning during development but the protein's involvement in these processes during anterior eye development has never been investigated. I show that Npnt has the correct spatiotemporal expression to potentially influence the migration and patterning of the vasculature and nerves that project to the anterior eye. Utilizing whole mount immunohistochemistry experiments, I found that Npnt is needed for the proper patterning of the choroid vasculature and for the proper projection profile of sensory nerve innervation into the anterior eye. I furthered these results using primary neuron cell culture experiments of dissociated trigeminal ganglia from embryonic mice, discovering that Npnt attenuates migration of sensory nerves in an integrin dependent manner. Finally, I definitively determined the developmental stage at which the corneal endothelial basement membrane, the Descemet's membrane (DM), is first formed with transmission electron microscopy. Npnt is expressed by the endothelial cells during development and is integrated into the membrane with changing spatial expression relative to other major basement membrane components. I found that Npnt is expressed not only during development of the membrane but is sustained throughout the life of an organism, suggesting it may be involved in the maintenance of the corneal endothelium or in the Descemet's membrane barrier functions. Overall, in this thesis, I identified a species-specific mechanism for how the extracellular matrix protein Npnt facilitates POM migration into the developing cornea. I expanded upon this by finding Npnt is a substrate for endothelial vasculature and sensory nerves during anterior eye formation. Identifying these functional roles for Npnt during development and noting its continued expression in the Descemet's membrane provides the basis for Npnt and its receptors being potential targets for corneal cell-matrix therapies.   Matthew Garis is inviting you to a scheduled Zoom meeting. item.description:
Wednesday, August 5, 2026 at 8:15 PM

Location: Miller Outdoor Theatre, 6000 Hermann Park Dr, Houston, TX, 77030, United States

Houston Shakespeare Festival, the city’s annual summer theater tradition, celebrates its 52nd season with performances of both The Tempest and Comedy of Errors on alternating nights at Miller Outdoor Theatre. Shakespeare’s The Tempest Exiled by her brother to a remote island and left to die, Prospera—the once loved Duchess of Milan and now an all-powerful sorceress—conjures a great tempest to wash ashore a ship of her enemies. With the power of magic, Prospera manipulates the survivors of the wreckage to weave a story of revenge, retribution, and reconciliation. Rich with spectacle, humor and wonder, Shakespeare’s final play brings audiences to a “brave new world ” where reconciliation is possible and humanity is renewed. Hosted by Miami’s Best Comedian Manny Garavito and Miami’s Best Master of Ceremonies Luke Prince, the show stirs up live comedy, tasteful crowd interaction, audience stories, terrible dating advice, red flags, green flags, first dates on the spot, and the hilarious realities of navigating Miami’s social scene. item.title: Advancing Genetic Code Expansion: From Genome-Wide Host Reprogramming to Innovative Biological Applications
item.description:
Thursday, August 6, 2026 at 6 PM

Location: BioScience Research Collaborative

  Speaker: Mengxi Zhang Doctoral Candidate Thesis Defense Department: Chemistry Location: BioScience Research Collaborative 282 Genetic code expansion (GCE) enables noncanonical amino acids (ncAAs) with diverse chemical and physical properties to be introduced into proteins at defined positions. This technology has provided valuable tools for protein labeling, functional regulation, biomolecular engineering and the investigation of biological processes. Despite the rapid development of GCE, many genetically encoded ncAAs have been demonstrated primarily at the level of protein incorporation, while their potential for solving broader biological and engineering problems remains underexplored. In addition, the production of ncAA-containing proteins is often limited by inefficient stop-codon suppression and by the cellular environment in which the orthogonal translation system operates. In this dissertation, we expand the applications of genetically encoded ncAAs in material engineering and live-cell imaging and investigate endogenous host factors that regulate ncAA-containing protein production. To introduce material-binding properties into proteins and living cells, 3,4-dihydroxy-L-phenylalanine (DOPA), a catechol-containing amino acid found in mussel adhesive proteins, was genetically incorporated into proteins at defined positions. Optimization of the DOPA incorporation system enabled the production of homogeneous DOPA-containing proteins with enhanced binding to a broad range of organic and inorganic materials. The material-binding capability of DOPA was further combined with intrinsically disordered proteins to generate adhesive antifouling proteins. Extending this strategy from proteins to living cells, DOPA was incorporated into a bacterial surface protein to substantially enhance bacterial attachment to different materials. The improved interaction between engineered bacteria and polyethylene terephthalate (PET) also facilitated bacterial degradation of PET, demonstrating the application of GCE in protein, material and cellular engineering. In addition to creating new protein functions, genetically encoded ncAAs can serve as compact probes for studying dynamic biological processes. A series of rotor-based fluorescent ncAAs was developed to monitor local protein microenvironment changes in living cells. Among these amino acids, AnapTh displayed strong responses to environmental polarity and viscosity. Computational redesign of an aminoacyl-tRNA synthetase enabled the site-specific incorporation of AnapTh into proteins in mammalian cells. Placement of AnapTh at selected residues allowed real-time monitoring of local environmental changes during the aggregation of human superoxide dismutase and Huntingtin proteins and during the clustering of STIM1 and CRY2. Distinct fluorescence responses observed at different incorporation sites revealed spatially resolved changes within individual protein regions, providing a method to visualize protein aggregation, clustering and their reverse processes with high spatial precision. While these studies demonstrate the functional potential of genetically encoded ncAAs, their broader utility depends on efficient and faithful ncAA-containing protein production. To investigate how the host cell contributes to this process, a genome-wide screen of the Escherichia coli Keio single-gene knockout collection was performed using a dual-fluorescent amber-suppression reporter. Nine gene deletions reproducibly altered reporter production across different ncAA incorporation systems, indicating that GCE is regulated by diverse endogenous cellular processes. Among these candidates, rplI, which encodes the 50S ribosomal protein bL9, was further investigated. Deletion of rplI reduced overall protein expression, increased relative amber-codon readthrough and decreased the translation elongation rate, linking ribosome dynamics to ncAA incorporation. Sequence Display was subsequently used to examine the sequence-function landscape of RplI and identified its C-terminal region as an informative target for further engineering. Together, this dissertation develops and explores important applications of genetically encoded ncAAs while providing insights into the host translational mechanisms that govern their incorporation.   (Department : Chemistry)

item.title: Quantifying Many-Body Contextuality with Multiplayer Nonlocal Games from Stabilizer Codes
item.description:
Thursday, August 6, 2026 at 7 PM

Location: Space Science Building

  Speaker: Wanbing Zhao Masters Candidate Thesis Defense Department: Physics & Astronomy Location: Space Science Building 301A Quantum contextuality is a fundamental property of quantum mechanics that captures the impossibility of reproducing quantum measurement outcomes from pre-existing classical values. Contextuality in few-particle quantum systems is commonly studied using Bell inequalities, but its emergence in large-scale, many-particle quantum systems remains poorly understood. Such many-body contextuality has attracted renewed attention in quantum information science through its formulation in terms of "nonlocal games" played with stabilizer codes, which are mathematically equivalent to Bell inequalities. However, work in this field has largely focused on determining whether such nonlocal games exhibit quantum advantage. To quantify many-body contextuality, we develop a systematic theory of nonlocal games defined on n-qubit stabilizer codes via nonlinear Boolean functions. The theory yields a universal upper bound of 7/8 on the classical value of such games that admit quantum advantage. For cyclic cluster states and toric codes, we prove that the classical values of the associated games approach 1/2 exponentially fast in n, resulting in exponentially large Bell-inequality violations. Going beyond these lattice examples, we show that exponential Bell-inequality violations are generic among random graph states, occurring with high probability over Erdős–Rényi ensembles with fixed edge probability p \in (0,1). These results provide a scalable path toward testing quantum contextuality on current and future quantum devices.   (Department : Physics & Astronomy)

Official Tickets Resale Tickets Comedy Cellar Las Vegas brings one of the most legendary names in stand-up comedy to the heart of Las Vegas. Located inside the Rio Hotel & Casino, this intimate comedy club is the West Coast home of New York City’s world-famous Comedy Cellar, the venue that helped launch the careers of comedy icons including Dave Chappelle, Chris Rock, Jon Stewart, Ray Romano, Amy Schumer, Aziz Ansari, and countless others. Unlike traditional comedy shows featuring a single headliner, Comedy Cellar presents a carefully curated lineup of professional comedians every night. Audiences can expect multiple performers during each show, featuring a mix of nationally touring headliners, television favorites, Comedy Central veterans, Netflix performers, and rising stars from around the world. No two shows are exactly alike, making every visit a unique experience. Surprise drop-in appearances from major comedians performing elsewhere in Las Vegas have become part of the club’s reputation, giving audiences the chance to see comedy superstars in an intimate setting. Event Details Venue: Comedy Cellar Las Vegas at Rio Hotel & Casino Location: 3700 W Flamingo Rd, Las Vegas, NV 89103 Show Schedule: Nightly performances throughout the year Age Requirement: Recommended for audiences 18+ due to mature comedy content About the Venue Opened in 2018, Comedy Cellar Las Vegas was designed to recreate the atmosphere and energy of the original Greenwich Village club that has become one of the most respected comedy venues in the world. The 300-seat showroom offers excellent sightlines and an intimate setting that allows audiences to experience stand-up comedy exactly as it was meant to be seen: up close and personal. The venue combines the excitement of a Las Vegas night out with the authentic feel of a classic New York comedy club. Guests can enjoy a comfortable showroom environment while watching some of the best comedians working today perform in a setting that encourages spontaneity, crowd interaction, and unforgettable moments. Conveniently located inside the Rio Hotel & Casino just minutes from the Las Vegas Strip, the venue offers easy access for both tourists and local comedy fans. What to Expect Expect a fast-paced evening featuring multiple comedians performing throughout the show. The Comedy Cellar is known for showcasing a wide variety of comedic styles, from observational humor and storytelling to sharp social commentary, crowd work, and cutting-edge stand-up. Whether you’re discovering a future comedy star or watching a seasoned veteran perfect their craft, every show delivers the authentic comedy club experience that has made the Comedy Cellar one of the most respected brands in stand-up comedy. For comedy fans visiting Las Vegas, Comedy Cellar is widely considered one of the best places in the city to experience live stand-up comedy any night of the week.

item.title: 52nd Annual Houston Shakespeare Festival: The Comedy of Errors at Miller Outdoor Theatre
item.description:
Thursday, August 6, 2026 at 8:15 PM

Location: Miller Outdoor Theatre, 6000 Hermann Park Dr, Houston, TX, 77030, United States

Houston Shakespeare Festival, the city’s annual summer theater tradition, celebrates its 52nd season with performances of both The Tempest and The Comedy of Errors on alternating nights at Miller Outdoor Theatre. Shakespeare’s Comedy of Errors Shakespeare’s riotous farce of mistaken identity, The Comedy of Errors, brings double trouble to the bustling port city of Ephesus when two sets of twins—separated at birth—unexpectedly cross paths, unleashing a whirlwind of mayhem and mirth. In this fast-paced comedy bursting with physical humor, outrageous confusion, and joyful surprise, husbands are mistaken for strangers, servants are denied their own names, and no one can tell friend from foe. As misunderstandings multiply and tempers flare, the laughter never lets up. Finding Your Seat at Miller Outdoor Theatre As always, all seats at Miller are free, but covered seating for popular evening shows usually requires a free assigned ticket reserved 24 hours in advance. Official Tickets Resale Tickets Comedy Cellar Las Vegas brings one of the most legendary names in stand-up comedy to the heart of Las Vegas. Located inside the Rio Hotel & Casino, this intimate comedy club is the West Coast home of New York City’s world-famous Comedy Cellar, the venue that helped launch the careers of comedy icons including Dave Chappelle, Chris Rock, Jon Stewart, Ray Romano, Amy Schumer, Aziz Ansari, and countless others. Unlike traditional comedy shows featuring a single headliner, Comedy Cellar presents a carefully curated lineup of professional comedians every night. Audiences can expect multiple performers during each show, featuring a mix of nationally touring headliners, television favorites, Comedy Central veterans, Netflix performers, and rising stars from around the world. No two shows are exactly alike, making every visit a unique experience. Surprise drop-in appearances from major comedians performing elsewhere in Las Vegas have become part of the club’s reputation, giving audiences the chance to see comedy superstars in an intimate setting. Event Details Venue: Comedy Cellar Las Vegas at Rio Hotel & Casino Location: 3700 W Flamingo Rd, Las Vegas, NV 89103 Show Schedule: Nightly performances throughout the year Age Requirement: Recommended for audiences 18+ due to mature comedy content About the Venue Opened in 2018, Comedy Cellar Las Vegas was designed to recreate the atmosphere and energy of the original Greenwich Village club that has become one of the most respected comedy venues in the world. The 300-seat showroom offers excellent sightlines and an intimate setting that allows audiences to experience stand-up comedy exactly as it was meant to be seen: up close and personal. The venue combines the excitement of a Las Vegas night out with the authentic feel of a classic New York comedy club. Guests can enjoy a comfortable showroom environment while watching some of the best comedians working today perform in a setting that encourages spontaneity, crowd interaction, and unforgettable moments. Conveniently located inside the Rio Hotel & Casino just minutes from the Las Vegas Strip, the venue offers easy access for both tourists and local comedy fans. What to Expect Expect a fast-paced evening featuring multiple comedians performing throughout the show. The Comedy Cellar is known for showcasing a wide variety of comedic styles, from observational humor and storytelling to sharp social commentary, crowd work, and cutting-edge stand-up. Whether you’re discovering a future comedy star or watching a seasoned veteran perfect their craft, every show delivers the authentic comedy club experience that has made the Comedy Cellar one of the most respected brands in stand-up comedy. For comedy fans visiting Las Vegas, Comedy Cellar is widely considered one of the best places in the city to experience live stand-up comedy any night of the week.

item.title: HXD Week: Beyond the Buzz
item.description:
Friday, August 7, 2026 at 12 PM

Location: Architecture Center Houston, 902 Commerce St., Houston, TX, 77002, United States

Beyond the Buzz: What Design Week Reveals About the Future of Interior Architecture Every year, Chicago Design Days and NeoCon introduce hundreds of new furniture products, materials, finishes, and workplace design concepts. But which innovations represent meaningful shifts in interior architecture—and which are simply this year’s aesthetic trends? This session examines key observations from Chicago Design Week through three lenses: ephemeral trends, enduring shifts, and emerging innovations. Participants will explore how circular design principles are reshaping furniture planning and specification, how neuroinclusive design is influencing occupant well-being, and how manufacturers are responding to evolving expectations around sustainability, flexibility, material transparency, and human-centered design. Rather than showcasing the latest products, this course provides architects and designers with a practical framework for evaluating furniture and interior design innovations, helping them distinguish what’s new from what’s next—and determine which ideas will have lasting impact on the health, safety, welfare, and performance of the built environment. AIA Credit: 1.0 LU|HSW About the presenters: Caryn Ogier, AIA, RID, LEED AP, PMP Kimiko Designs Director of Furniture Planning is the Director of Furniture Planning at Kimiko Designs, where she helps clients align furniture strategy with business goals, user needs, and long-term sustainability. With more than 25 years of experience in architecture, interiors, and project management, Caryn specializes in furniture planning, circular design,and lifecycle stewardship for workplace and healthcare environments. A lifelong learner and self-proclaimed furniture woobie, Caryn is passionate about translating emerging ideas into practical project outcomes. She has helped shape Kimiko’s circularity movement and brings a unique perspective that connects design, project management, and implementation, helping owners, architects, and designers turn good ideas into spaces that perform better over time. Necia E. Bonner, RID, NCIDQ, IIDA, CHID, CDF, LEED AP Perkins&Will Principal and Director of Health & Science Interiors Necia Bonner is a Principal and the Director of Health & Science Interiors for Perkins&Will’s Houston studio, where she leads interior design strategy for some of the most complex healthcare, research, and science environments in the country. With more than 25 years of experience dedicated exclusively to high-performance interiors, she has worked across a broad spectrum of specialized facilities, including academic medical centers, community hospitals, behavioral health facilities, public health agencies, private clinics, research laboratories, vivaria, and corporate science campuses. A Certified Healthcare Interior Designer and Certified Design Futurist, Necia is recognized for her expertise in translating complex clinical, operational, and regulatory requirements into innovative environments that support the future of healthcare delivery and scientific discovery. She is a respected leader within the design profession and a frequent advocate for advancing healthcare and science environments through design leadership, education, and professional service. Necia has served in numerous leadership roles with IIDA, the AIA Committee on Architecture for Health, the Texas Association for Interior Designers, and currently serves on the board of Texas Women in Healthcare. item.title: HXD Week: Electrolit U.S. Headquarters Tour
item.description:
Friday, August 7, 2026 at 2 PM

Location: Private: Electrolit U.S. Headquarters, 3201 Allen Parkway, Houston, TX, 77010, United States

A collaborative team of architects based in Guadalajara and Houston has designed the U.S. headquarters of Mexican beverage brand Electrolit. The structure they chose to begin their journey in Houston—a low-slung, formerly industrial Spanish Revival slab located on the banks of Buffalo Bayou—resonated with the ethos and cultural identity of the company. The objective from the outset was to create a contemporary workspace imbued with the sophistication and relaxed character of residential architecture, balancing the industrial nature of the existing building with a warm palette of natural materials reminiscent of Mexican living. With this ambition in mind, the architects stripped the existing concrete structure down to its bones, correcting and repairing some of the abuses that it had undergone during its many lives. The proposal consists of a series of volumetric, light wooden boxes that house smaller programs and inhabit the industrial space as sculptures, creating and lending proportion to the spaces around them. The main entry leads into a foyer bounded on one side by a monumental wood-clad staircase. Past this stair, the space opens into a double-height lounge and flexible workspace. The stair leads to a mezzanine where the CEO’s office and a meeting room overlook the office. Throughout, diffused natural light emitted by glass-block windows is supplemented by existing skylights. The team worked to deploy warm tones and raw materials in order to strike a balance between the rough and the delicate. The result, aided by the thoughtful use of natural light, is a relaxed and subdued atmosphere that stands in opposition to the stridence of contemporary corporate vernacular. Through its careful consideration of existing conditions and its balance between the industrial and the intimate, the project also manages to strike a different balance, between the company’s origins in Mexico and its new location in Houston. Winner of the 2026 AIA Houston Design Award for Interior Architecture. Learn more here!

From AIA Houston

item.title: Thalamo-cortical evoked effective connectivity to guide personalized neuromodulation in epilepsy
item.description:
Friday, August 7, 2026 at 6 PM

Location: BioScience Research Collaborative

  Speaker: Jasper Wang Masters Candidate Thesis Defense Department: Electrical and Computer Engineering Location: BioScience Research Collaborative 875 Thalamic deep brain stimulation (DBS) has emerged as a promising treatment for drug-resistant epilepsy. Besides the anterior nucleus of the thalamus (ANT), the only FDA-approved target, the centromedian nucleus (CM) and pulvinar have also been shown to be promising targets. However, outcomes vary both across and within stimulation targets, and to date there is no consensus on the optimal stimulation site within each thalamic nucleus. Here, we hypothesized that effective connectivity, as quantified by thalamo-cortical evoked potentials (TCEPs), could guide personalized DBS target selection. We recorded scalp EEG responses to single-pulse electrical stimulation delivered via thalamic DBS electrodes in 15 epilepsy patients. Voxel-based linear mixed-effects modeling was applied to TCEP data to generate stimulation-response maps with high spatiotemporal resolution. We provided group-level TCEP stimulation-response maps of the CM and pulvinar, and showed that pulvinar and CM subregions selectively engage distinct cortical networks, detectable with non-invasive scalp EEG. The pulvinar showed a medial-to-lateral gradient: medial pulvinar mapped to anterior temporal cortex, middle pulvinar to mid-temporal cortex, and lateral pulvinar to parietal and posterior temporal cortex. Lateral-dorsal CM showed strong connectivity to frontocentral regions. Finally, we demonstrated a significant correlation between acute TCEP response and long-term seizure reduction rate within the same patient cohort, supporting the clinical translational potential of this approach.   Zoom link: https://www.google.com/url?q=https://riceuniversity.zoom.us/j/93695667394?pwd%3DBlRXICqUVKI2MZvD1W2ySZwFarWfq1.1&sa=D&source=calendar&ust=1785182094516539&usg=AOvVaw321gy5b1gZlvJrgy-BIX9J (Department : Electrical and Computer Engineering)

Born and raised in San Francisco, Ali broke through with her wildly popular Netflix specials Baby Cobra (2016) and Hard Knock Wife (2018), both filmed while she was visibly pregnant — a bold and hilarious choice that became her signature. Her fourth Netflix special, Ali Wong: Single Lady (2024), earned her a Golden Globe Award and a Critics Choice TV Award nomination. About the Venue The Arlene Schnitzer Concert Hall — lovingly called “The Schnitz” by Portlanders — is one of the Pacific Northwest’s most treasured performance spaces. Situated in the heart of downtown Portland at 1037 SW Broadway Ave, this magnificent 2,776-seat venue is part of the Portland’5 Centers for the Arts complex. Originally constructed in 1928 as the Portland Public Theatre, the hall was meticulously restored and reopened in 1984. Its stunning Italian Baroque architecture, ornate interior details, and world-class acoustics create an unforgettable atmosphere for live performances. Every seat in the house offers excellent sightlines to the stage. The venue features orchestra, mezzanine, and balcony seating levels, along with a full bar, concessions, and accessible seating options. item.title: First Fridays Presents Tina Cardona
item.description:
Friday, August 7, 2026 at 7:30 PM

Location: Inprint House, 1520 W Main St, Houston, TX, 77006, United States

Free and open to the public Doors @ 7 pm Pop-up poet @ 7:30 pm Featured poet @ 7:40 pm Open mic @ 8:15 pm Inprint is proud to serve as the host for the First Fridays Reading Series. The First Fridays Reading Series is the oldest poetry series in Houston and was organized by Robert Clark from 1975-2019. Today, First Fridays events are curated and hosted by local community members. The August featured reader will be Tina Cardona, a community maker for Houston poets as a co-founder of hotpoet.org. She is a psychotherapist, yoga teacher, earth advocate, dog guardian, soothsayer, mother and partner, and is also in a long-standing, conflictual relationship with poetry. You can find her wandering at dawn and at dusk muttering with trees. The opening pop-up poet will be Michael J. Galko, a retired scientist and active poet from Houston. He is the artist responsible for ‘haiku house’, a residential art installation consisting of hundreds of original wood-burned and painted haiku. He was a finalist in the 2020 Naugatuck River Review and the 2022 Bellevue Literary Review poetry contests. Recent poems appear in Spillway Magazine, Atlanta Review, Silk Road Review, and Plainsongs, among other journals. Houston Shakespeare Festival, the city’s annual summer theater tradition, celebrates its 52nd season with performances of both The Tempest and Comedy of Errors on alternating nights at Miller Outdoor Theatre. Shakespeare’s The Tempest Exiled by her brother to a remote island and left to die, Prospera—the once loved Duchess of Milan and now an all-powerful sorceress—conjures a great tempest to wash ashore a ship of her enemies. With the power of magic, Prospera manipulates the survivors of the wreckage to weave a story of revenge, retribution, and reconciliation. Rich with spectacle, humor and wonder, Shakespeare’s final play brings audiences to a “brave new world ” where reconciliation is possible and humanity is renewed. Unlike traditional comedy shows featuring a single headliner, Comedy Cellar presents a carefully curated lineup of professional comedians every night. Audiences can expect multiple performers during each show, featuring a mix of nationally touring headliners, television favorites, Comedy Central veterans, Netflix performers, and rising stars from around the world. No two shows are exactly alike, making every visit a unique experience. Surprise drop-in appearances from major comedians performing elsewhere in Las Vegas have become part of the club’s reputation, giving audiences the chance to see comedy superstars in an intimate setting. Event Details Venue: Comedy Cellar Las Vegas at Rio Hotel & Casino Location: 3700 W Flamingo Rd, Las Vegas, NV 89103 Show Schedule: Nightly performances throughout the year Age Requirement: Recommended for audiences 18+ due to mature comedy content About the Venue Opened in 2018, Comedy Cellar Las Vegas was designed to recreate the atmosphere and energy of the original Greenwich Village club that has become one of the most respected comedy venues in the world. The 300-seat showroom offers excellent sightlines and an intimate setting that allows audiences to experience stand-up comedy exactly as it was meant to be seen: up close and personal. The venue combines the excitement of a Las Vegas night out with the authentic feel of a classic New York comedy club. Guests can enjoy a comfortable showroom environment while watching some of the best comedians working today perform in a setting that encourages spontaneity, crowd interaction, and unforgettable moments. Conveniently located inside the Rio Hotel & Casino just minutes from the Las Vegas Strip, the venue offers easy access for both tourists and local comedy fans. What to Expect Expect a fast-paced evening featuring multiple comedians performing throughout the show. The Comedy Cellar is known for showcasing a wide variety of comedic styles, from observational humor and storytelling to sharp social commentary, crowd work, and cutting-edge stand-up. Whether you’re discovering a future comedy star or watching a seasoned veteran perfect their craft, every show delivers the authentic comedy club experience that has made the Comedy Cellar one of the most respected brands in stand-up comedy. For comedy fans visiting Las Vegas, Comedy Cellar is widely considered one of the best places in the city to experience live stand-up comedy any night of the week.

item.title: 52nd Annual Houston Shakespeare Festival: The Comedy of Errors at Miller Outdoor Theatre
item.description:
Saturday, August 8, 2026 at 8:15 PM

Location: Miller Outdoor Theatre, 6000 Hermann Park Dr, Houston, TX, 77030, United States

Houston Shakespeare Festival, the city’s annual summer theater tradition, celebrates its 52nd season with performances of both The Tempest and The Comedy of Errors on alternating nights at Miller Outdoor Theatre. Shakespeare’s Comedy of Errors Shakespeare’s riotous farce of mistaken identity, The Comedy of Errors, brings double trouble to the bustling port city of Ephesus when two sets of twins—separated at birth—unexpectedly cross paths, unleashing a whirlwind of mayhem and mirth. In this fast-paced comedy bursting with physical humor, outrageous confusion, and joyful surprise, husbands are mistaken for strangers, servants are denied their own names, and no one can tell friend from foe. As misunderstandings multiply and tempers flare, the laughter never lets up. Finding Your Seat at Miller Outdoor Theatre As always, all seats at Miller are free, but covered seating for popular evening shows usually requires a free assigned ticket reserved 24 hours in advance. Learn more about getting free seated tickets at Miller. Admission Free. Learn more or reserve a free seated ticket. item.title: DroneArt Show: Harry Potter at Constellation Field
item.description:
Saturday, August 8, 2026 at 9 PM

Location: Constellation Field, 1 Stadium Dr, Sugar Land, TX, 77498, United States

DroneArt Show returns to Houston with an official Harry Potter light show in the sky at Constellation Field in Sugar Land. The show promises to be an unforgettable open-air spectacle as 1,200 illuminated drones recreate favorite characters and beloved moments from the Harry Potter films. As night falls, hundreds of synchronized illuminated drones take off and create shapes in the sky, moving in time with John Williams’ movie score played live in a 65-minute performance. Inspired by the Wizarding World, the show ensures every guest takes part in the experience with exclusive LED wristbands. The open air setting will have food and drink for sale. Plus—whether you’re sorted into houses Gryffindor, Hufflepuff, Ravenclaw or Slytherin—costumes and Wizarding World attire are highly encouraged. Admission Tickets start at $48; $28 for ages 3 to 11. item.title: Intoxication in British Literature, 1660-1760
item.description:
Monday, August 10, 2026 at 4 PM

  Speaker: Rowan Morar Doctoral Candidate Thesis Defense Department: English "Intoxication in British Literature, 1660-1760" argues for reading literary representations of intoxicants and altered states of mind, as a normative condition of Enlightenment life and a feature of literary representation itself. Drawing from social history, I trace how mass markets for drugs, such as plantation produced tobacco and spirits, as well as opium left their imprints on the works of key authors of British literary history—Lord Rochester, Aphra Behn, Daniel Defoe, and Charlotte Lennox. I argue that these writers from 1660-1760, the Restoration to the mid-Enlightenment period, represented the influx of colonially produced drugs that became fiscal necessities for statecraft in order to make tacit assumptions about everyday self-regulation, socialization, and politics visible. Profane appetites were as fundamentally changed in Britain as they were central to concepts of subjectivity in the violent colonial theaters producing the intoxicants for an era of taste and refinement. The construction of a subjective experience of intoxication in poems, the performance of drunkenness on the stage, the narrative accounts of inner consciousness affected by rum or tobacco, wine or opium—all offer means for seeing double: the work of intoxicants on literature and literary intoxication during an increasingly global era of mass intoxication.   https://riceuniversity.zoom.us/s/92686072682 (Department : English)

From Rice University - Open to the Public

item.title: An Apparatus for Quantum Simulation with Rydberg Atoms
item.description:
Monday, August 10, 2026 at 6 PM

Location: Brockman Hall for Physics

  Speaker: Brent Kruzel Doctoral Candidate Thesis Defense Department: Physics & Astronomy Location: Brockman Hall for Physics 300 This thesis presents the design, construction, and characterization of a new experimental platform for quantum simulation using ultracold strontium-88 Rydberg atoms. The apparatus was developed to support future optical-tweezer based experiments that realize synthetic dimensions through coherent millimeter-wave coupling between neighboring Rydberg states while providing the optical access, electric- and magnetic-field control, and state-sensitive detection required for precision measurements. A new science chamber was designed and integrated with laser cooling, selective field ionization, and charged-particle detection systems, while electromagnetic simulations were used to optimize millimeter-wave delivery and field uniformity. Experimental characterization of the completed apparatus includes measurements of static electric-field compensation, millimeter-wave polarization purity, and coherent Rydberg spectroscopy through Rabi and Ramsey techniques. In addition, analysis methods were developed to extract relative Rydberg-state populations from selective field ionization signals, and new high-precision microwave spectroscopy measurements were incorporated into an updated determination of the quantum defect Rydberg-Ritz parameters for the singlet S, P, and D Rydberg series of strontium. Together, these developments establish the experimental and analytical foundation for future quantum simulation experiments on this new apparatus.   (Department : Physics & Astronomy)

item.title: Mercury Fund Day at the Ion: AI Product Design and Distribution: Lessons from Building at Scale
item.description:
Tuesday, August 11, 2026 at 3:30 PM

Location: Ion – Forum Stairs, 4201 Main St., Houston, TX, 77002, United States

Welcome to “Mercury Fund Day at the Ion” – a program series hosted by the Ion and Mercury, where software founders can connect with mentorship at Houston’s HQ for innovation. What is it: Mercury Fund Day, previously known as Software Day, is a monthly series driving the support, inspiration, and connections needed to help startups on their path to rapid, sustainable growth. Each month, Mercury Fund Day will include office hours (by application), a keynote session, and networking. Each month will include a new speaker and topic covering the latest trends and breakthroughs in software technology and practical advice for founders. From AI to blockchain and guidance on fundraising, explore topics that are relevant for your company’s journey. Afterward, join us for a networking happy hour at Second Draught, brought to you by Gunderson Dettmer, where you can connect with fellow entrepreneurs, investors, and industry professionals, forging connections that could shape the future of your venture. This month’s topic: Every enterprise software company says it’s going AI-first. Few have actually rebuilt the product, the pricing model, and the team around it. Join us at Mercury Day at Ion Houston on August 11th for a working conversation with three people doing that rebuild from different seats: Mustafa Ali (Growth, Twilio), Zafir Khan (Product, Meta), and Salim Gheewalla (Founder, Utilitise, which replaced the IT help desk with AI that fixes problems before anyone notices). Panelists will get into what separates a great AI product experience from a clunky one, when AI should run invisibly in the background versus prompt the user directly, what consumption-based pricing does to a SaaS business model, and how hiring changes when a team is building AI-native from day one. Hosted by Heath Butler of Mercury Fund, panelists include: Mustafa Ali – Growth @ Twilio Zafir Khan – Product @ Meta (former Mercury Intern) Salim Gheewalla – Founder @ Utilitise Prior to the fireside chat, a select group of early-stage software startups will participate in office hours. Over the course of 2-hours, first-time entrepreneurs looking for guidance or seasoned founders needing help tackling tough challenges will have access to a group of curated mentors from the Mercury network and gain insights and guidance tailored to their needs. Startups are invited to apply to participate here. “Mercury Fund Day at the Ion” isn’t just an event – it’s a catalyst for growth and collaboration. Don’t miss this opportunity to be part of Houston’s thriving tech ecosystem. Join us as we bring together leading mentors, promising startups, and like-minded Houstonians focused on transformative software innovations.

item.title: Lunchtime Learning (Virtual)
item.description:
Wednesday, August 12, 2026 at 12 PM

Location: Zoom

Virtual Lunchtime Learning sponsored by the Committee on the Environment (COTE)   First Safe, then Circular: optimizing material health with Cradle to Cradle Certified® If you are being asked to evaluate the material health of products and aren’t sure where to start, this session is for you! We’ll dive into the basics of material health for designers, including major classes of chemicals of concern, chemical assessments, and how designers can use certifications as they evaluate products. This presentation details the methodology and requirements for the Cradle to Cradle Certified® products program and how designers can use it to specify materials that are healthy in a project and across a supply chain. We’ll explore how Cradle to Cradle Certified®, as a fully digitized program, makes it easy for designers to find reliable material health information to deliver meaningful sustainability benefits on every project.   Speaker: Ren DeCherney, Director of Built Environment Ren is a licensed interior designer who uses her first-hand experience of the complexities of the building industry to help designers and manufacturers translate their sustainability pledges into reality. Prior to joining the Institute as Director of Built Environment, she worked in Portland as a designer, where she took her firm PVC-free, making them the first firm in Portland to make such a commitment. She was then the Director of Industry Transparency at Source, a digital materials platform, where she synthesized design team needs and industry trends to integrate sustainability seamlessly into the design process. This included building various user tools, growing strategic partnerships, and developing all of the sustainability filters on the platform. She then worked at the International Living Future Institute, overseeing the Declare and Living Product Challenge programs. There she worked with both designers and manufacturers to understand the current market incentives for sustainable practices and how to implement sustainability strategy into everyday practices.   AIA Credit: 1.0 HSW GBCI Credit: self-report  

From AIA Houston

item.title: Essays on the Energy Transition in Electricity Markets
item.description:
Wednesday, August 12, 2026 at 9 PM

Location: Baker Hall

Renewable energy is restructuring the generation mix in electricity markets, simultaneously driving thermal retirement, substantially suppressing wholesale energy prices when and where they are generating, and redirecting investment toward new technologies such as battery storage to compensate for their effects. This dissertation studies all three channels in the Electric Reliability Council of Texas (ERCOT) market. Each chapter takes a different angle and methodology: structural estimation of retirement decisions, analytical equilibrium theory for renewable dynamics, and reduced-form spatial analysis of investment composition. The first chapter estimates a dynamic discrete choice model of retirement for natural gas and coal-fired generators in ERCOT, treating exit as an irreversible optimal stopping problem under forward-looking expectations. All 45 observed exits in the estimation panel occur at strictly positive operating profit, consistent with retirement as a forward-looking continuation-value decision rather than a current-period margin trigger. The retirement decision in the model has two channels: a current-period flow payoff in which operating profit and age enter directly, and a forward-looking continuation value that summarizes the expected path of future operating profit. Operating profit is constructed at unit resolution from a 15-minute spark-spread payoff that combines real-time nodal locational marginal prices (LMPs) and fuel-cost indices (Henry Hub for gas units, delivered coal costs for coal units). Ancillary service revenue recovered from the ERCOT 60-Day Security-Constrained Economic Dispatch (SCED) record is added, and pro-rated fixed operating and maintenance costs are subtracted. Operating profit enters the flow payoff positively and significantly (coefficient +0.653, t-statistic 3.15 under a random-effects specification). Generator age enters negatively (-0.510), marginal under random effects and strongly significant without them. Wind and solar shape retirement decisions through the operating-profit transition kernel rather than the flow payoff. Their persistence in the kernel transmits into continuation values, which is how the model captures the effect of renewable trajectories on exit. Both kernel coefficients are negative (wind -0.157, solar -0.030), reflecting the merit-order erosion of incumbent operating profit, with wind the stronger channel and solar the weaker. Two counterfactual exercises explore the implications of the estimated structural model. A wind-versus-solar dose-response varies zonal renewable shares and shows how marginal renewable expansion reshapes the composition of the surviving fleet. A forward projection built from the April 2026 ERCOT Generator Interconnection Status report calibrates expected renewable buildout. Through 2035, the fleet's existing age distribution dominates retirement, while the renewable buildout contributes only marginally. The structural estimates and counterfactuals provide a reference point for policymakers and market planners assessing how the dispatchable thermal fleet evolves under continued renewable buildout in ERCOT. The second chapter extends the analytical framework of Green and Leautier (2015) in two directions. First, we derive a complete set of marginal impact results under a Feed-in Premium (FiP), an extension they identified as an open problem. Under FiP, renewable producers receive the wholesale price plus a fixed premium per MWh and curtail output when the price falls below the negative of the premium. The results cover the long-run generation mix, the per-MW market value of renewables, the equilibrium tax, and the required marginal subsidy. Because renewables avoid producing in the worst-priced states, the per-MW market value of renewable capacity falls more slowly as renewable penetration grows under FiP than under a fixed-price Feed-in Tariff. Second, we adapt the framework to the ERCOT market, which uses an Operating Reserve Demand Curve (ORDC) to set scarcity prices in lieu of a forward capacity market. ERCOT's ORDC applies a scarcity adder to the real-time energy price when operating reserves are low, calibrated to the expected cost of the curtailment those reserves would prevent. Throughout the chapter's sample period (2019-2023), the ORDC operated as an ex post adder to the energy clearing price under sequential energy and ancillary service auctions, rather than as a co-optimized shadow value within a single security-constrained dispatch. We adopt the economic logic of Hogan (2013), who derived the ORDC for a co-optimized setting, and adapt it to this pre-co-optimization institutional environment. The principal theoretical result is that the ORDC does not directly affect the rate at which renewable per-MW values fall with renewable penetration. Where infra-marginal conventional generators are at capacity, marginal changes in reserves shift rents to those generators without altering the rate at which renewable value declines. The ORDC's effect on renewable values therefore operates indirectly, through the equilibrium generation mix. A calibration exercise using ERCOT data confirms three qualitative findings. The FiP reduces the per-MW subsidy needed to sustain renewable entry and slows the rate at which the per-MW value of renewables falls. Nuclear capacity exits the equilibrium at approximately 80 GW of wind under FiT and at approximately 77 GW under ERCOT's ORDC-based market structure, while the FiP retains nuclear across the full simulated range. The earlier exit reflects a demand-channel asymmetry that the chapter establishes analytically and the calibration confirms. The combined FiP-ERCOT case is the policy-relevant one for ERCOT, since the federal Production Tax Credit shares the FiP's premium-on-top-of-price structure. Under this regime, the calibration shows substantially slower per-MW value decline than without the FiP, with nuclear retention preventing the abrupt acceleration that follows nuclear exit. This analysis bridges the analytical framework of Green and Leautier (2015) with the scarcity-pricing logic of Hogan (2013), and the ERCOT calibration provides its empirical interpretation. The third chapter estimates a discrete choice model of generator investment across ERCOT's four load zones over 2011-2024. Developers choose among five technologies (wind, solar, combined-cycle gas, open-cycle gas, and battery storage), grouped into dispatchable and non-dispatchable segments. Entry composition is estimated with a multinomial logit in the Berry (1994) log-odds inversion, with operating profit instrumented by national fuel-cost shifters and rival characteristics. Fixed cost deters entry (-3.63, p < 0.001) and federal subsidies shift composition toward the subsidized technologies (+2.29, p < 0.001). Both results are stable when year and zone fixed effects are added and when the model is re-estimated as a Poisson count model, which retains the zone-years with no entry that the log-odds inversion must drop. Entry shows no detectable response to annual energy margins. Gas-fired entry falls well below what observed payoffs alone would predict. The results quantify the mapping from ERCOT's price signals to the technology composition of investment and inform the resource adequacy debate.

item.title: Jesus Benavente: NUESTROWORLD
item.description:
Thursday, August 13, 2026 at 12 AM

Location: DiverseWorks, @ 5601 B Navigation Blvd & Various Locations, 5601 B Navigation Blvd, Houston, TX, 77011, United States

Opening Thursday, August 13, 2026 | 6 – 8 pm DiverseWorks @ 5601 B Navigation Blvd NUESTROWORLD is a satirical solo installation by Brooklyn-based artist Jesus Benavente. Featuring newly commissioned works, NuestroWorld opens on Thursday, August 13, 2026, transforming 5601 B Navigation Blvd, Houston, TX 77011 into a fictional visitor center for NuestroWorld, encouraging guests to explore Houston beyond the gallery walls and experience the city as an amusement park. The installation will be on view through September 13, 2026, with a closing party on September 11. Gallery hours are Thursday – Saturday, 12 – 6 pm. Admission is free. Through satire and spectacle, NuestroWorld examines how cities construct identity through tourism, branding, memory, and myth, inviting audiences to reconsider Houston’s past and present. The exhibition draws inspiration from pivotal moments in Houston and Texas history, including the opening of the Astrodome and Astroworld in the late 1960s, Selena’s iconic Houston Livestock Show & Rodeo performances in the 1990s, and the folklore surrounding Santa Anna’s capture following the Battle of San Jacinto in 1836, highlighting the city’s recurring cycles of ambition, folly, and heartbreak. The title plays on “Astroworld” and uses Spanglish to create the phrase “The World Is Ours,” reframing Houston’s cultural mythology through humor, nostalgia, and critical reflection. Opening Reception Thursday, August 13, 6 – 8 pm Artist and Curator Talk: 6:45 pm Closing Party Friday, September 11, 2026, 6 – 8 pm 7 pm: special performance by CTS Trio – Queen of Tejano & Latin Tribute ARTIST BIO: Jesus Benavente is a visual artist based in Brooklyn, New York, and born in San Antonio, Texas. Benavente earned an MFA from Rutgers University and attended Skowhegan School of Painting and Sculpture. Recent exhibitions and performances include Reception Rome, Italy; the Whitney Museum of American Art, New York; Queens Museum; LTD Los Angeles; Performa 13, New York; Acre Projects, Chicago; Chinati Foundation, Marfa; the Neuberger Museum of Art, Purchase, NY; Shin Museum of Art, South Korea; Vox Populi, Philadelphia; and Socrates Sculpture Park, New York. Website: http://jesusbenavente.net Instagram: @testotesto3  

From DiverseWorks

item.title: Physics-informed machine learning for reconstructing dark matter and neutrino signals in TPCs
item.description:
Thursday, August 13, 2026 at 3 PM

Location: Herman Brown Hall

  Speaker: Ivy Li Doctoral Candidate Thesis Defense Department: Physics & Astronomy Location: Herman Brown Hall HBH 227 Dual-phase xenon time projection chamber (TPC) experiments such as XENONnT are sensitive probes of dark matter and neutrinos, but as these detectors grow more complex and data-intensive, distinguishing signals of interest from backgrounds depends on improved data handling and novel analysis techniques. This thesis introduces multiple machine learning applications toward position and energy reconstruction for these detectors. Initial studies of semi-supervised autoencoders with partially interpretable latent spaces and recurrent neural networks for correcting ionization signal waveforms demonstrated their limitations from the lack of physics constraints. Continuous normalizing flow models were developed to learn the electric field inside TPCs with physics-motivated constraints built into their architecture. With a learned electric field, the flow model is able to correct for field distortions in position reconstruction. Compared to traditional methods, the flow model reduces calibration data requirements by 50 times, its physics-informed architecture ensures that the learned electric field is curl-free, and the improvement in position reconstruction consequently improves charge yield estimation across the energy range of interest for both WIMP and neutrinoless double beta decay searches. Finally, the thesis presents a demonstration of the flow's applications towards a probabilistic fiducial volume in next-generation experiments.   Zoom: https://riceuniversity.zoom.us/j/93454420074?pwd=0ePCCADW4tBbylIlayywSkxCBMyTgp.1 (Department : Physics & Astronomy)

item.title: Everyday Self-Defense: Building Confidence Through Boundaries & De-escalation
item.description:
Thursday, August 13, 2026 at 5 PM

Location: Third Ward Jiu-Jitsu, 2016 Emancipation Ave, Houston, TX, 77003, United States

In this self-defense session, the instructor, Sarah Degar, Jiu Jitsu black belt, and architect at GSMA, will share her unique approach to personal safety, focusing on two key objectives: setting boundaries and de-escalating potential uncomfortable situations. After demonstrating key techniques, attendees will partner up to practice, with the instructor offering guidance to each group. The first part of the session will teach participants how to navigate unwanted physical contact in everyday situations, particularly with people they know. In professional and social contexts, it can be challenging to assert boundaries—especially for many women who already worry about being perceived as “unreasonable.” The instructor will address simple strategies to divert this contact to maintain comfort and autonomy. For example, a colleague approaches for a hug or puts an arm around the waist to pose for a photo. Attendees will be empowered to practice subtle yet effective ways to establish personal space without confrontation. The second part of the session will address more serious scenarios, where the potential for physical harm exists. Whether the concern comes from someone familiar or not, de-escalation is crucial. Participants will learn techniques to create and maintain a safe distance, keep a steady stance to avoid being easily pushed or pulled, and how to break free from various types of holds. The session will wrap up with interactive games designed to reinforce the skills learned, making it fun and memorable while encouraging participants to continue practicing on their own. Doors Open 5p Class 5:30p – 6:30p Social to follow

item.title: Illuminating the dynamics of magmatic systems: from bubbles to the lithosphere, from a computer to the lab
item.description:
Thursday, August 13, 2026 at 7 PM

Location: Keith-Wiess Geological Laboratories

  Speaker: Gaetano Ferrante Doctoral Candidate Thesis Defense Department: Earth, Environmental and Planetary Sciences Location: Keith-Wiess Geological Laboratories KWGL 123 Volcanoes are the surface manifestation of Earth's great geodynamic forces. They provide an invaluable window into geologic processes that are hidden from direct observation, yet they represent a significant hazard for millions of people around the world. Investigating the dynamics of volcanic systems is thus crucial to better understand our planet and improve assessments of volcanic hazard. Volcanic processes occur over a wide range of spatial and temporal scales, motivating the use of correspondingly diverse methodologies to investigate their dynamics. In this thesis, I will employ experiments, numerical modeling and data analysis to address some of the most fundamental, yet widely disputed, questions in volcanology. One of the major controls on the eruptive style and ensuing hazard of a volcano is the viscosity of its magma. Among other factors, gas bubbles suspended in the magma can either increase or decrease its viscosity, strongly influencing eruptive dynamics. In Chapter 1, I will present results from rheology experiments conducted on natural pumice samples to understand how bubbles affect the viscosity of magma. I will propose a new and unambiguous constitutive equation for the viscosity of bubbly magmas that can be used to better model volcanic eruptions and lava flows. Magmatic systems can extend for tens of kilometers from the asthenosphere, where magma is produced, to the Earth's surface, where it is eventually erupted. Whether volcanoes are controlled from the bottom-up or from the top-down is still a major question in volcanology. In Chapter 2, I will couple a numerical model of magma flow at the lithospheric scale with surface-available observations collected during the past 30 years at Kīlauea volcano (Hawaiʻi), to shed light on the dynamics of its magmatic supply pathway. "Why do eruptions end?" is a fundamental, yet overlooked question in volcanology. In 2018, Kīlauea experienced its largest eruption in more than 200 years of history, providing an unprecedented set of observations that helped volcanologists improve our understanding of caldera-forming eruptions. More than 8 years after the start of the eruption, the reasons underlying its sudden and unexpected conclusion still remain, for the most part, a mystery. In Chapter 3, I will jointly analyze a diverse set of geophysical data collected during Kīlauea's 2018 eruption to shed light on its progression and enigmatic end, providing a framework to interpret the evolution of past and future caldera-forming eruptions.   https://riceuniversity.zoom.us/j/4149242694?pwd=YWZsUDhEVWthT3E3R041SkpNMk5uQT09&omn=99605727293 (Department : Earth, Environmental and Planetary Sciences)

item.title: Bayesian Inference and Medical AI: From Period Estimation to Cardiac Volume Prediction
item.description:
Thursday, August 13, 2026 at 8 PM

  Speaker: Tony Gao Doctoral Candidate Thesis Defense Department: Statistics This thesis presents three projects unified by their focus on developing and applying statistical and machine learning methods for robust parameter estimation across different scientific domains. In the first project, the accurate estimation of the periodicity of variable stars is important for understanding their physical properties and behaviors. While current methods may give accurate point estimates, uncertainty quantification is often missing. We develop a fast semi-parametric Bayesian model for period estimation that provides principled uncertainty quantification. We establish asymptotic consistency of the period estimator and apply the method to variable stars from the OGLE II project. The subsequent two projects focus on automating diagnosis in medical imaging with Artificial Intelligence (AI) models. Emerging AI models provide accurate left ventricular volume estimates from echocardiograms (echo) compared to human experts when echo is used as the reference. However, a combination of poor image quality, human error, and volume assumptions of echo may not provide accurate estimation. We therefore use cardiac magnetic resonance imaging (CMR) estimates as the reference standard because they are more accurate and reproducible. We apply and assess two state-of-the-art foundational models in a novel Houston Methodist cohort in which patients underwent both echo and CMR within 24 hours of each other. Finally, we develop a custom AI model fine-tuned on these data, which substantially improves upon the off-the-shelf models and performs comparably to human experts. https://riceuniversity.zoom.us/j/93352464646?pwd=qDte6U4fVL4UU90ACeCbLyhiz8vxgj.1   (Department : Statistics)
