item.title: OVERFLOW RADIO: Šakotayišol Nunuš Constellation
item.description:
Saturday, October 3, 2026 at 12 AM

Location: DiverseWorks – Gallery @ MATCH, 3400 Main Street, Houston, TX, 77002, United States

October 3-24, 2026DiverseWorks Gallery @ MATCHGallery Hours: 12 noon – 6 pm, Thursday-Saturday Celebrated for her large-scale social choreographies, Emily Johnson / Catalyst’s newest project, Overflow Radio is a performance, skill-share, planting of 1000 trees, and radio transmission from across territories. In conjunction with the world premiere of Overflow Radio in Mni Sóta Makoce (Minneapolis), DiverseWorks hosts an Overflow Radio: Šakotayišol Nunuš Constellation here in Houston. Over 24 non-consecutive hours, we will gather in-person to listen to twelve First Nations and Indigenous authors, poets, and scholars live-broadcasting from their home territories and First Nations. We’ll pay attention to other scales, other forms, other knowledges. We’ll traverse together, transcending colonial borders, languages and time. We’ll feast and celebrate the making of community, as we practice our shared commitment to creating our possible futures, as we gather what we need to know. The program is developed in collaboration with Emily Johnson and local Indigenous and Native artists to include talks, skill-shares, listening gatherings, an exhibition, and performances by Aveda Adara, Chiara Beaumont, Chichi, Karen Navarro, Aryn Ward and Monica Villarreal, with additional participating artists and community partners to be announced. The project is co-organized by DiverseWorks, Emily Johnson / Catalyst, and the participating artists and partners. Programs (please check back for updated information)DW Art + Climate CONVERSATIONS: Emily Johnson, 6:30 pm July 29Opening Event and Reception: 5 – 8 pm, October 3Listening Gatherings: 12noon – 6 pm (specific hours TBD), October 9-12Diverse Discourse Lecture & Studio Visits: Mary Bourdeaux: October 16-19 / Lecture 6 pm, Oct. 17 AcknowledgementsOverflow Radio is a National Performance Network Creation & Development Fund Project commissioned by Roy and Edna Disney / CalArts Theater (REDCAT) and co-commissioned DiverseWorks, MASS MoCA and University of Minnesota Department of Theatre Arts & Dance, more information at www.npnweb.org. Overflow Radio is developed through creative residencies provided by MASS MoCA, John and Mabel Ringling Museum of Art, Roy and Edna Disney / CalArts Theater, University of Minnesota’s Imagine Fund with support from the McKnight Foundation, and Danspace Project with support from the New York State DanceForce, a partnership program of the New York State Council on the Arts. Overflow Radio is created with generous support from First Peoples Fund, Howard Gilman Foundation, Harkness Foundation for Dance, and the New England Foundation for the Arts’ National Dance Project with lead funding from the Doris Duke Foundation and The Mellon Foundation. Emily Johnson / Catalyst is fiscally sponsored by Producer Hub. Image: Emily Johnson / Catalyst, Quilt Being Star, worn by Ty Fierce Matteba, photo by Two Hawks Young.

item.title: Inprint Ayad Akhtar Reading
item.description:
Monday, October 5, 2026 at 7:30 PM

Location: Alley Theatre, 615 Texas Avenue, Houston, TX, 77002

General admission tickets will go on sale on Tuesday, September 15, 2026 at 12 pm. Season tickets are on sale here. Ayad Akhtar will read from his new novel The Radiance, followed by an on-stage conversation led by a local author/journalist. The evening will conclude with a book sale and signing. The event is presented as part of the 2026/2027 Inprint Margarett Root Brown Reading Series.  Pulitzer Prize winner Ayad Akhtar’s new novel The Radiance is “simply put, a work of genius. Through unforgettable characters Akhtar explores the nature of memory and of the soul, while the unfolding tale builds tension and anticipation like a whodunit” (Abraham Verghese). It has been named one of the New York Time‘s “Novels Everyone Will Be Talking About in 2026.” A mysterious accident along a country road sparks an awakening and an investigation in Akhtar’s most daring work yet—a visionary novel of spiritual transformation in an age of fracture. Akhtar’s work as a novelist and playwright has been published and performed in over two dozen languages. He is the winner of the Pulitzer Prize for Drama for his play Disgraced, which was also nominated for the Tony Award for Best Play. His other Broadway plays include McNeal, Junk, and The Who & The What. Akhtar is also the author of the novels American Dervish, a Kirkus Reviews Best Book of the Year, and Homeland Elegies, called “a tour de force” by The Washington Post. In 2021, he was named the New York State Author by the New York State Writers Institute, succeeding Colson Whitehead.

From Inprint Houston

item.title: Texas Colloquium on Distributed Learning (TL;DR 2026)
item.description:
Thursday, October 8, 2026 at 10 AM

Location: O'Connor Building for Engineering & Science

Date: Thursday & Friday, October 8-9, 2026About:The workshop onFuture-proof Distributed/Federated Learningwill take place October 8-9, 2026, in Houston, USA, at Rice University. To attend both days, we recommend arriving to Houston on the evening of October 7. We expect around 100 participants, including domestic and international researchers working in distributed learning, multi-agent systems, federated learning, optimization, large-scale AI systems, and responsible agentic AI. Read more about the the speakers and itinerary on the event website (https://sites.google.com/rice.edu/tldr2026/)! Aim of the Workshop: The purpose of this workshop is to gather leading researchers on Federated Learning, Distributed Computing and Large-Scale ML at Rice University; the workshop will discuss and focus on efficient distributed learning algorithms on how to train such large models using less costly/specialized computing platforms. Topics of interest include, but are not limited to, Systems and infrastructure, Fairness, Hardware for on-device distributed learning, Privacy concerns, Optimization advances, Theoretical contributions, and Applications of distributed learning.Support: The National Science Foundation, the Rice University Creative Venture Fund, the Rice University Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering, the Rice University Department of Mechanical Engineering, the Rice University Department of Computer Science, and the Ken Kennedy Institute, and the CORE-AI OWLS Cluster.

From Rice University - Open to the Public

Event details

item.title: Across Two Seas Symposium
item.description:
Thursday, October 8, 2026 at 10 AM

Location: Moody Center

Across Two Seas brings together scholars, curators, artists, and community members for a multi-day symposium at Rice University on Black subjectivities across the medieval and early modern Mediterranean, Islamic world, and Indian Ocean. Through panels, film screenings, public conversations, and interdisciplinary dialogue, the symposium explores how Black subjects were represented in artistic, literary, and documentary sources and how these representations were shaped by trade, travel, religion, knowledge-making, and cultural exchange. By connecting Europe, North Africa, the Arabian Peninsula, East Africa, India, and Southeast Asia, Across Two Seas expands the geography of premodern race studies and places the Indian Ocean at the center of conversations too often framed primarily through Europe. The symposium invites broader publics to consider how histories of Blackness were made across multiple regions, media, and worlds.

From Rice University - Open to the Public

item.title: Distinguished Lecture with Francesco Bullo
item.description:
Thursday, October 8, 2026 at 9 PM

Location: Duncan Hall

RSVP to Attend (https://k2i.wufoo.com/forms/distinguished-lecture-with-francesco-bullo/): The distinguished lecture is from 4:00-5:00 PM, followed by a social from 5:00-6:00 PMSpeaker: Professor Francesco Bullo (https://fbullo.github.io/)— Professor of Mechanical Engineering at UC Santa Barbara Talk Title: TBD When: Thursday, October 8, 2026 @ 4:00-6:00 PM Central Where: Auditorium, Duncan Hall, Rice University (6100 Main St., Houston, TX 77005) Parking: Paid parking will be available in Founder's Court Lot or the Entrance 3 (COB) Garage. Visit the Rice University Campus Maps webpage (https://www.rice.edu/campus-maps) for directions. Organizers: Ken Kennedy Institute (https://kenkennedy.rice.edu/)Speaker Bio Francesco Bullo is Distinguished Professor and Mosher Endowed Chair of Mechanical Engineering at the University of California, Santa Barbara, CA, USA. He received the Laurea degree in Electrical Engineering from the University of Padova, Italy, in 1994, and the Ph.D. degree in Control and Dynamical Systems from the California Institute of Technology, Pasadena, CA, in 1998. His research interests include contraction theory, network systems, neural networks, and mathematical neuroscience. He is the author or coauthor of Geometric Control of Mechanical Systems (Springer, 2004), Distributed Control of Robotic Networks (Princeton, 2009), Lectures on Network Systems (KDP, v1.7, 2024), and Contraction Theory for Dynamical Systems (KDP, v1.3 2026). He served as IEEE CSS President and SIAG CST Chair. He is a Fellow of ASME, IEEE, IFAC, NetSci, and SIAM

item.description:
Friday, October 9, 2026 at 12 AM

Location: Brookwood Gift & Garden Center & Café, 1502 FM 1489, Brookshire, TX, 77423, United States

Brookwood Horticulture Workshop: Succulent Pumpkin Centerpiece A Fall Favorite You Won’t Want to Miss! Autumn is calling—and so are the pumpkins! Join us for one of Brookwood’s most beloved seasonal traditions: the Succulent Pumpkin Centerpiece Workshop, led by Horticulture GM Robert Grove. In this hands-on experience, you’ll blend the rich textures of fall with the fresh beauty of succulents to craft a one-of-a-kind centerpiece that’s perfect for your table—or to gift to someone special! 🍂 What’s Included: Create & Take: Design your very own succulent pumpkin masterpiece to take home and enjoy all season long. Expert Guidance: Learn arrangement tips and care techniques from Brookwood’s own horticulture pro, Robert Grove. Flexible Scheduling: Choose from 10 sessions over two days—making it easy to fit into your busy fall calendar. Celebrate the beauty of the season with friends, creativity, and purpose—surrounded by the plants grown and cared for by the incredible Citizens of Brookwood®. 📍 Hosted at Brookwood Gift & Garden Center🌟 Let your fall décor tell a story of creativity, community, and heart. Dates: Friday & Saturday, October 9 & 10, 2024 Time: Choose from Five Sessions Each Day: 9-10 AM 10:15-11:15 AM 11:30 AM-12:30 PM 1-2 PM 2:30-3:30 PM Location: Horticulture Building, Behind the Garden Center Registration: $45 (plus tax) covers all the materials needed to make your own centerpiece. Space is limited, so reserve your spot today! Grab your tickets today!   Dining Options: Lunch at The Brookwood Café: Available Friday and Saturday from 11 AM – 2 PM. Lunch reservations are required and can be made here: https://bit.ly/BWOpenTable Please note: Food is not included with the event ticket.   Join us for an inspiring afternoon of horticultural know-how, flavorful food, and a purposeful take-home gift! Reserve your spot today! When you’re in the checkout cart, please click the “ORDER NOTE” option to let us know if you’d like to sit with specific guests. Be sure to include their names so we can arrange seating accordingly. Please note that our luncheon tables seat up to 8 guests.   Thank you for supporting the beloved adults with disABILITIES who live and work at Brookwood! Changing the way the world thinks about adults with disabilities Visit our Events Calendar for the full schedule of Brookwood’s upcoming events.   CANCELLATION POLICY: Full Refund (100%): Requests made 7 or more days before the event date will be eligible for a full refund. item.title: Across Two Seas Symposium
item.description:
Saturday, October 10, 2026 at 10 AM

Location: Moody Center

Across Two Seas brings together scholars, curators, artists, and community members for a multi-day symposium at Rice University on Black subjectivities across the medieval and early modern Mediterranean, Islamic world, and Indian Ocean. Through panels, film screenings, public conversations, and interdisciplinary dialogue, the symposium explores how Black subjects were represented in artistic, literary, and documentary sources and how these representations were shaped by trade, travel, religion, knowledge-making, and cultural exchange. By connecting Europe, North Africa, the Arabian Peninsula, East Africa, India, and Southeast Asia, Across Two Seas expands the geography of premodern race studies and places the Indian Ocean at the center of conversations too often framed primarily through Europe. The symposium invites broader publics to consider how histories of Blackness were made across multiple regions, media, and worlds.

From Rice University - Open to the Public

item.title: Inprint Hernan Diaz Reading
item.description:
Monday, October 12, 2026 at 7:30 PM

Location: Stude Concert Hall, Rice University, Entrance #18 & #20, 6100 Main St., Houston, TX, 77005, United States

General admission tickets will go on sale on Monday, September 21, 2026 at 12 pm. Season tickets are on sale here. Hernan Diaz will read from his new novel Ply, followed by an on-stage conversation led by a local author/journalist. The evening will conclude with a book sale and signing. The event is presented as part of the 2026/2027 Inprint Margarett Root Brown Reading Series.  Described by Lauren Groff as a “narrative genius,” Hernan Diaz is the Pulitzer Prize-winning and bestselling author of the novel Trust, named one of the New York Times’s Best 100 Books of the 21st Century and currently being developed as a limited series for HBO. His literary work is celebrated for its genre-bending reinvention of American mythology and its complex exploration of wealth, capitalism, and isolation. His first novel, In the Distance, was a finalist for the Pulitzer Prize and the PEN/Faulkner Award. His work has been translated into 37 languages. After rewriting America’s past in his two previous novels, from 1920s Wall Street to the 19th century western frontier, Diaz turns to the future with his new novel Ply. A combination of Dickensian odyssey, family drama, and scientific thriller, Ply examines the place of technology in the American imagination. Centuries from now, the state has been dismantled, and humans are reinventing social bonds and learning new ways to coexist with nature. Following a childhood defined by loss, survival, and found family, an orphan grows up to become a “pincher,” someone who steals electricity from the grid to sell it on the black market. “Diaz brilliantly envisions how love, trust, and loyalty can remain when freedom and justice have collapsed and makes every page exhilarating and meaningful” (Library Journal, starred review).

From Inprint Houston

item.title: ESCRITORES EN LA CASA: Ezequiel Zaidenwerg
item.description:
Thursday, October 15, 2026 at 7:30 PM

Location: Inprint House, 1520 W Main St, Houston, TX, 77006, United States

Inprint recibe al autor argentino Ezequiel Zaidenwerg para presentar su nueva novela en verso, Fantasma escritor. Tras la presentación, Zaidenwerg conversará sobre su obra con un escritor local. Esta presentación forma parte de la serie de Inprint Escritores en la casa. Todas las presentaciones de Escritores en la casa son gratis y están abiertas al público.  Ezequiel Zaidenwerg nació en Buenos Aires en 1981. Es autor de varios libros incluyendo los poemarios Doxa (2007) y La lírica está muerta (2011, 2017). Además, es traductor de Mark Strand, Ben Lerner, Anne Carson, Weldon Kees, Robin Myers, Joseph Brodsky, Mary Ruefle, João Cabral de Melo Neto,  Brenda Hillman, Kay Ryan y Emily Dickinson, entre otros y otras. Es miembro fundador del colectivo de acción poética Como Un Lugar y envía diariamente por mail poemas traducidos a través de su newsletter El poema de hoy. Su primera novela, Fantasma Escritor, fue elogiada por Fernanda Trías, quien escribió: “Ezequiel Zaidenwerg dirige su inteligencia inquieta hacia los fantasmas que nos constituyen: la familia, la lengua, el duelo, el deseo, la herencia. Zaidenwerg, que con su newsletter El poema de hoy ha hecho de la poesía y la traducción una forma de encuentro colectivo, entrega ahora una primera novela íntima y luminosa, vulnerable y formalmente viva. Este es un libro sobre la traducción como una manera de estar en el mundo: el arte de escuchar aquello que nos rodea y de encontrar las palabras que acaso nos permitan decir yo.” Esta serie de lecturas es posible gracias a la Rita Mallett Blasser Foundation

From Inprint Houston

item.title: Inprint Cool Brains! Series presents Elizabeth Acevedo
item.description:
Sunday, October 18, 2026 at 2 PM

Location: TX

Free and open to the public Free copies of Anger Is Only a Shadow for the first 100 families Appearance by celebrated Houston writer Jasminne Mendez Meet the author followed by a book sale and signing Bus scholarships available for student groups – full scholarships for public schools, partial scholarships for private schools upon availability. For information, email info@inprint.org Books available through Kindred Stories And more! The 2026/2027 Inprint Cool Brains! Series proudly presents National Book Award winner and renowned poet Elizabeth Acevedo, sharing her new YA novel Anger Is Only a Shadow. Known for YA novels filled with poetry, humor, and heart, Elizabeth Acevedo is the New York Times-bestselling author of The Poet X, which won the National Book Award for Young People’s Literature, the Michael L. Printz Award, the Pura Belpré Award, the Carnegie medal, the Boston Globe–Horn Book Award, and the Walter Award. She is also the author of With the Fire on High, which was named a best book of the year by the New York Public Library, NPR, Publishers Weekly, and School Library Journal; and Clap When You Land, which was a Boston Globe–Horn Book Honor book and a Kirkus finalist. Acevedo is a National Poetry Slam Champion and served as the 2022 Young People’s Poet Laureate. “An irresistible story of family connection, resilience, and loyalty” (Kirkus starred review), Anger Is Only a Shadow is Acevedo’s powerful new YA novel in prose and poetry. Lil is anything but small. She’s rebellious, she’s loyal; she’s figuring out what kind of good person she wants to be, or if she wants to be a good person at all. But more than anything? Lil wants to be free. When her instinct for freedom leads to another stay in D.C. juvenile detention, Lil knows she’s lucky to just be on probation. But judgment, guilt, and an ankle monitor weigh heavily on her, and she can’t shake that pinned-down feeling. The only person who might understand is her big brother, Aldwin. Except he’s more distant now than just the hundred miles from his college. As her court hearing ticks closer, a question looms over Lil as the missed phone calls and strange texts from her brother pile up: will she stay put, or put her future freedom on the line? “A striking and nuanced portrait of the realities of juvenile detention and mental illness” (Publisher’s Weekly starred review) and “intensely genuine” (The Bulletin of the Center for Children’s Books starred review), Anger Is Only a Shadow a white-knuckle journal to self-understanding and doing the right thing, no matter the cost.

From Inprint Houston

item.title: CSWGS Gray/Wawro Lecture - Siri Suh
item.description:
Wednesday, October 21, 2026 at 11 PM

The Center for the Study of Women, Gender, and Sexuality in collaboration with the Department of Sociology at Rice University invites you to a Gray/Wawro Lecture in Gender, Health, and Wellbeing bySiri Suh (https://www.sirisuh.com/) Associate Professor of Sociology Brandeis UniversityWednesday, October 21, 2026 5:00 PM Reception 6:00 PM Lecture This event is free and open to the public.  Advance registration is required.  The event venue will be confirmed here closer to the date of the lecture. Siri Suh is an Associate Professor of Sociology at Brandeis University with research interests in the global governance of maternal and reproductive health. Her book, Dying to Count: Post-Abortion Care and Global Reproductive Health Politics in Senegal (https://www.rutgersuniversitypress.org/dying-to-count/9781978804548/) (2021, Rutgers University Press), received the 2022 Eileen Basker Memorial Prize for outstanding research in gender and health from the American Anthropological Association's Society for Medical Anthropology. In 2022, Suh launched the Into Women's Hands (https://www.intowomenshands.org/) project to explore the role of misoprostol in the pharmaceuticalization of reproductive health in francophone Africa. With funding from the Hewlett Foundation, Suh collaborates with faculty and graduate students at Joseph Ki-Zerbo University in Burkina Faso and Cheikh Anta Diop University in Senegal to conduct ethnographic research on the use and circulation of misoprostol in health facilities, pharmacies, informal drug markets, social media networks, and with NGOs and professional associations. Suh received her PhD in Sociomedical Sciences and her MPH from Columbia University.  Learn more about the Gray/Wawro Lecture Series on our website (https://cswgs.rice.edu/lectures).  This event counts toward the required 12 colloquium events for the CSWGS Graduate Certificate.

From Rice University - Open to the Public

item.title: Engineers in the C-Suite: Leslie M. Duke, Chair and CEO of Burns & McDonnell
item.description:
Thursday, October 22, 2026 at 11 PM

Location: Duncan Hall

ABOUT THE SPEAKER   A proven leader and collaborator, Leslie Duke built her career on aligning business strategies with client needs, building business in new and existing marketplaces by driving innovation and developing next-generation leaders to advance the firm's vision and values. Safety is at the core of every decision she makes.  Her top commitment as CEO is to the safety and well-being of employee-owners, clients, partners and the communities the firm serves. Prior to her role as chair and CEO, Leslie served as regional president and general manager of the firm's South Central Region.  Leslie helped expand the firm's regional client base from an initial Houston client to over 650 local, regional and national clients in numerous marketplaces such as power utility, petrochemical, refining, manufacturing and space exploration.  Leslie's integral role in launching Burns & McDonnell's engineer-procure-construct (EPC) delivery method led to the development and successful execution of numerous multimillion-dollar projects.  During her tenure, Leslie's region delivered over $4 billion in revenue for environmental, consulting, engineering, procurement and construction services. Leslie joined Burns & McDonnell in 1999 as a structural engineer and advanced through a series of leadership roles, including opening offices in Austin, Dallas and Fort Worth, Texas and Raleigh, North Carolina where she served as general manager.  She became a senior vice president in 2014 and, in 2016, was named the firm's first female president. Leslie earned a bachelor's degree in civil/structural engineering from Texas Tech University and was named a Texas Tech Distinguished Engineer in 2018.  She is an emeritus member of the Dean's Council for the university's School of Engineering. Leslie and her husband, Travis, have two children. She is a member of the United Way of Greater Kansas City board, The Economic Club of Kansas City and the Civic Council of Greater Kansas City.  She and Travis served as co-chairs of the Ronald McDonald House of Kansas City Spark of Hope Gala.    __ABOUT THE ENGINEERS IN THE C-SUITE SPEAKER SERIES Hosted by the Rice Center for Engineering Leadership (RCEL) (https://www.rcelconnect.org/), Engineers in the C-Suite features executives and thought leaders from technology organizations who uniquely employ or depend on engineers.  These accomplished leaders share experiences in navigating change and how engineers can equip themselves to lead the way.  Through this series, learn about how products and workplaces are being disruptively transformed through technological advancements, and how engineers are expected to not just adapt to but lead this transformation. Previous Engineers in the C-Suite speakers include:Mark Lashier, Chairman and CEO, Phillips 66 (Fall 2025) (video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=9Oql-Yp92lg&t=19s (https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=9Oql-Yp92lg&t=19s)) Sandra Johnson, CEO of SKJ Visioneering and former CTO of IBM Africa (Fall 2024) (video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=wJlT3xvHhIk) (https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=wJlT3xvHhIk))Antonio Neri, CEO of Hewlett Packard Enterprise (Spring 2024) (video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=yBwYQvrfM14&t=4s) (https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=yBwYQvrfM14&t=4s))Jim Whitehurst, former CEO of Red Hat and President of IBM (Fall 2023) (video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ty2M4Dw9pcg) (https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ty2M4Dw9pcg))  REGISTRATION Check back soon for RSVP link!

item.title: Park to Port Bike Ride
item.description:
Saturday, October 24, 2026 at 8 AM

Location: Bayou Parkland, 6532 Almeda Rd, Houston, TX, 77021, United States

Hermann Park Conservancy’s 12th annual Park to Port Bike Ride is set for Saturday, October 24. The 20-mile round-trip bike ride takes cyclists from Hermann Park’s Bayou Parkland along the Bayou Greenway trail all the way to Mason Park, near the Port of Houston. Enjoy the turn-around party, but be sure to save some energy for a well-deserved post-ride party under the Bill Coats Bridge! Park to Port is open to riders of all skill levels and is not a race. Whether you are an experienced cyclist or are riding just for fun, you can go at your own pace on this scenic city journey. Your participation in Park to Port supports Hermann Park Conservancy and its stewardship efforts for one of Houston’s most beloved parks while promoting the ever-growing Bayou Greenway trail system. Register and learn more at the following link: 12th Annual Park to Port Bike Ride. Early bird pricing is available until August 17. SPECIAL OFFER: Save $10 on registration when you sign up for BOTH the Park to Port Bike Ride and Run in the Park! Bundle deal is available via the link above. Information on Run in the Park can be found here.

From Hermann Park Conservancy
